But an investigator interviewed the first officer, who told them that the initial take-off roll and taxi was normal. The the co-pilot "noticed a deviation from the center line of the runway and a sudden left turn," Sumwalt said. Passengers on Sunday described the chaos inside the plane after the plane came to rest.  Watch survivor describe crash on blog » . Continental spokeswoman Julie King, however, told CNN that she was unaware of any announcement of engine problems on board the flight. Sumwalt agreed, saying, "I don't have any information, no one has come to us that they knew of a problem" before the accident.

**DENVER, Colorado** — A Continental Airlines jetliner veered off a runway and caught fire during takeoff at Denver International Airport Saturday evening, injuring dozens of passengers but resulting in no fatalities, officials said.

Continental Flight 1404, a Boeing 737-500 bound for Houston, was carrying 110 passengers and five crew members when the accident occurred around 6:18 p.m. local time. The aircraft skidded off the left side of the runway during its takeoff roll, coming to rest in a ravine as fire erupted along the right side of the fuselage.

## Injuries and Evacuation

Officials reported that 38 people were transported to area hospitals with injuries ranging from minor to serious. The Denver Health Medical Center treated several passengers, including the flight's captain, who suffered more significant injuries.

Passengers described a terrifying sequence as the aircraft left the runway and emergency slides deployed.

"There was this violent shaking, and then we just went off to the side," said one passenger who was seated near the middle of the aircraft. "The next thing I knew, there was fire outside the windows on the right side, and people were scrambling to get to the exits on the left."

Another passenger recounted the chaotic evacuation. "It was dark, it was cold, and we just ran from the plane. People were helping each other in the snow. We're just grateful to be alive."

Temperatures at the airport were near freezing at the time, with reports of gusty winds in the area.

## NTSB Investigation

The National Transportation Safety Board dispatched a "go team" to Denver to lead the investigation. Investigators recovered the aircraft's flight data recorder and cockpit voice recorder, which were sent to the NTSB laboratory in Washington for analysis.

In early briefings, NTSB officials indicated that the aircraft never became airborne, veering off the runway during the takeoff attempt. Investigators said they would examine multiple factors, including weather conditions, wind data, the aircraft's mechanical systems, and crew actions.

"We are looking at everything," an NTSB spokesman said at a news conference. "That includes the weather, the runway conditions, the performance of the aircraft, and the human factors involved. It is far too early to draw any conclusions about the cause."

Investigators noted strong crosswind conditions were being examined as a potential factor. Wind gusts reported in the area raised questions about whether they may have contributed to the loss of directional control.

The aircraft sustained substantial damage, with the fire consuming portions of the right side of the fuselage and the landing gear collapsing during the excursion.

## Airline and Airport Response

Continental Airlines issued a statement expressing concern for those affected. "Our thoughts are with the passengers and crew of Flight 1404. We are cooperating fully with the NTSB and all authorities investigating this accident."

Denver International Airport temporarily closed the affected runway but continued operations on others. Airport officials praised the response of emergency crews, who reached the scene within minutes.

Aviation safety experts noted that the survival of all aboard reflected improvements in aircraft design and crew training. "The fact that everyone got out of that aircraft is a testament to modern safety standards and evacuation procedures," one analyst said.

The NTSB indicated its full investigation could take several months to a year to complete, with a preliminary report expected in the coming weeks.

*This is a developing story and will be updated as more information becomes available.*
